description: The bar chart titled “Evaluation Based on Different Tasks” visually compares the performance accuracy of three different model configurations—“Base,” “RMU with Enhanced GCG,” and “RMU”—across two distinct evaluation tasks: “MCQ Eval” and “Generation Eval.” The vertical y-axis represents “Accuracy,” scaled from 0.0 to 0.6 in increments of 0.2, while the horizontal x-axis categorizes the two evaluation tasks. For “MCQ Eval,” the “Base” model (red bar) achieves the highest accuracy at 0.644, followed by “RMU with Enhanced GCG” (light green, 0.539), and “RMU” (light yellow, 0.299). In “Generation Eval,” the “Base” model again leads with 0.597, followed by “RMU with Enhanced GCG” at 0.263, and “RMU” at 0.106. The bars are grouped by task, with each group containing three adjacent bars corresponding to the three models, as indicated by the legend below the chart. The chart visually emphasizes that the “Base” model consistently outperforms the unlearning variants across both tasks, and that “RMU with Enhanced GCG” generally performs better than “RMU” alone, though both fall significantly behind the base model. The data supports the paper’s claim that existing LLM unlearning evaluations may be inconclusive, as even enhanced unlearning methods show substantial performance degradation compared to the unmodified model.
